overview: Single-ward prospective observational study over 12 weeks from 5 October 2026: daily reconciliation of screening entries against ward lists for every eligible patient-shift, direct observation on a sample of shifts, and follow-up of every positive screen to medical review. Practice is not changed.
population: All patients aged 65 or over present on the ward during a nursing shift; patients receiving end-of-life care are excluded from the denominator as the policy exempts them.
exposure: Shift type (day, evening, night), weekday or weekend, dementia diagnosis, severe hearing or vision loss, and side-room care, recorded by the research nurse from the ward list and the notes.
procedures: Each weekday morning the research nurse reconciles the previous 24 hours (and weekends on Mondays) against the ward's shift lists. Each week she observes four day or evening shifts and two night shifts, following eight patients chosen by a fixed bed rota and recording whether the screening questions were asked. For every positive screen she records the time of the first documented medical review. If she sees an unrecognised delirium she informs the nurse in charge, and the event is recorded.

outcomes.name: Screen completion per eligible patient-shift
outcomes.measure: Proportion of eligible patient-shifts with a documented RDS-4 screen, reconciled against the shift list
outcomes.why: Directly measures adherence to the ward policy.

outcomes.name: Documented screens confirmed by observation
outcomes.measure: Proportion of documented screens on observed shifts at which the screening questions were asked
outcomes.why: Corrects for screens recorded but not done (claim c2).

outcomes.name: Positive screens reviewed within 24 hours
outcomes.measure: Proportion of positive screens with a documented medical review of mental state within 24 hours
outcomes.timing: Each positive screen, followed to review or discharge
outcomes.why: Screening helps the patient only if a positive result leads to review.

outcomes.name: Time from ward arrival to first screen
outcomes.measure: Hours from ward arrival to the first documented screen
outcomes.why: The policy requires a first screen within 12 hours.

outcomes.name: Patients woken for a screen at night
outcomes.measure: Observed night screens performed on a patient who was asleep
outcomes.why: Screening should not add to sleep disruption, itself a delirium risk.

feasibility: About 6,500 eligible patient-shifts and 72 observed shifts in 12 weeks fit the research nurse's 0.4 FTE; no forms are added for ward nurses.
biasMitigation: Fixed bed rota for choosing observed patients
Observed and unobserved shifts compared for record-based completion to estimate observer effect
Written operational definition of a completed screen fixed before the first shift
Dementia and sensory loss taken from admission documentation before observation starts

biasFlags.label: Observer effect
biasFlags.note: Nurses may screen more on observed shifts; compared with unobserved shifts.

biasFlags.label: Misclassified dementia status
biasFlags.note: Dementia may be under-recorded; the research nurse checks admission notes.

biasFlags.label: Selection of observed patients
biasFlags.note: Bed rota rather than observer choice.

flags: Six pre-specified factors; no data-driven additions
parsimony.simplestPath: One ward, one completion measure per patient-shift, a fixed observation sample and the review step.

theoreticalFramework: None beyond describing the screening pathway step by step; a behavioural framework can be chosen once failure points are known.
summary: 12-week prospective observation with one primary completion outcome, two secondary, one process and one balancing measure.
